findings.claim: The safeCount field on the spaces listing used to count one row per chain but now counts distinct Safe addresses across chains, while the Swagger description on get-space.dto.entity.ts still says it is the total count of Safes in the space, so a Safe on 3 chains now reports safeCount 1 even though GET /v1/spaces/:id/safes returns 3 entries, and a client comparing the two or labeling the count per-network would get inconsistent numbers with no indication the meaning changed.

The ApiProperty description for safeCount does not reflect that the value now represents distinct Safe addresses across chains rather than a count of per-chain rows; it should be updated to describe the new semantics, and the PR description should mention the change so API clients are aware.

With SafeSeatsGuard removed, a workspace that is already over its seat limit only receives its 402 rejection after encryptRows has made one KMS call per Safe in the payload and after a transaction has acquired the advisory lock, whereas previously the guard rejected the request before incurring any KMS calls; since the payload array has no maximum length, an admin retrying a large over-limit batch would repeatedly pay this cost.

The Safe payload schema (SpaceSafesSchema) has no maximum array length, which allows arbitrarily large batches to be submitted and processed (including KMS encryption calls) before any over-limit check occurs; adding a max size constraint or a cheap pre-check before encryption would bound this cost.
